decisions.title: SAF is allowed only at an import/export gateway; the engine core never sees content:// URIs
decisions.value: Engine core operates only on workspaces backed by real file paths; SAF code lives only in ARC-FS-4 (gateway) and is DEFERRED.
decisions.reason: Directive from the product owner; content:// grants are revocable and cannot support atomic apply, isolation or ownership checks.

decisions.title: WorkspaceFileSystem delegates to (is mounted on) the existing ProjectFileSystem; it is not a parallel implementation
decisions.value: RealWorkspaceFileSystem wraps an injected com.anvex.core.engine.ProjectFileSystem (verified signature in core:engine, implemented by core:android RealProjectFileSystem). It adds only: content digests, CAS snapshots, fork/materialize. It exposes the wrapped ProjectFileSystem to the Anvex ActionDispatcher in the adapter layer.
decisions.reason: RealProjectFileSystem already provides PathSanitizer checks, canonical-path confinement, atomic tmp+fsync+rename writes and symlink-safe delete/walk; duplicating them would fork security-critical code.

decisions.title: Port is named WorkspaceFileSystem; implementation RealWorkspaceFileSystem
decisions.value: com.anvex.agents.fs.WorkspaceFileSystem (port, in agents-core) and com.anvex.agents.fs.RealWorkspaceFileSystem (agents-fs).
decisions.reason: Avoids name collision with com.anvex.core.engine.ProjectFileSystem and com.anvex.core.android.fs.RealProjectFileSystem, which already exist in Anvex 4.15.2.

decisions.title: Core uses a root-relative RelPath model; no absolute paths; version control and shell are separate ports
decisions.value: WorkspaceFileSystem has no getAbsolutePath. RelPath validates (no .., no absolute, no NUL/control/bidi, segment <= 255, total <= 4096). VersionControlPort and ShellPort are implemented in the Android layer against the same real root.
decisions.reason: An absolute path in the core invites File use; GitLite needs a root File, so it is reached through a port, not through the filesystem interface.

decisions.title: Snapshot = content-addressed store (CAS) plus manifest; a hash alone is never a snapshot
decisions.value: Blobs are stored by SHA-256 under <agentsRoot>/cas/<aa>/<sha256>. A Manifest maps RelPath to (blobId,size,kind); SnapshotId = SHA-256 of the canonical manifest. restoreSnapshot rebuilds the tree from blobs and verifies every blob hash on read. Copy-on-write is not used: app-private storage offers no reflink API.
decisions.reason: Directive: a manifest must be backed by recoverable content. Limits (documented): empty directories, symlinks and mode bits are not captured.

decisions.title: MVP merge policy: line-based three-way merge, automatic only for non-overlapping regions, overlap is a conflict
decisions.value: Base = snapshot taken at fork; ours = current integration workspace; theirs = agent result. Hunks that touch the same or adjacent base lines conflict. Identical changes on both sides are clean. Edge-case table in 04_ARCHITECTURE/03_backend_architecture.md.
decisions.reason: Conservative policy chosen over heuristics; false conflicts are recoverable, silent wrong merges are not.

decisions.title: Ownership and permissions are enforced by the core Policy Engine and Integrator, not by ports
decisions.value: Ports perform mechanical operations only. PolicyEngine evaluates every ChangeSet entry before the Integrator applies it. Decisions: ALLOW, DENY, ESCALATE, DEFER with precedence DENY > ESCALATE > DEFER > ALLOW; missing evidence is never ALLOW.
decisions.reason: Directive; mirrors the PFP Runtime Enforcement Contract fail-closed sequence.

decisions.title: Every agent output is untrusted input and is validated before it can be applied
decisions.value: ChangeSetValidator rejects: invalid RelPath, symlink/mode entries, size or count over limits, paths outside the task write grant, sensitive paths, and malformed structure. Free-text messages never reach a shell or policy decision.
decisions.reason: Directive and PFP Runtime Enforcement Contract; validation is code, not prompt text.

decisions.title: agents-core is pure JVM with zero Anvex dependencies; the scheduler is a deterministic state machine
decisions.value: Module :feature:agents-core depends only on the Kotlin standard library. Scheduler contract: next(state, event) returns (state, commands). Coroutines appear only in agents-runtime.
decisions.reason: Allows the whole decision logic to be compiled and tested without Gradle, Android or a device.

decisions.title: Language: Kotlin 2.0.21
decisions.value: Kotlin 2.0.21, jvmTarget 17.
decisions.reason: Matches gradle/libs.versions.toml of Anvex 4.15.2.

decisions.title: Framework: Kotlin standard library and kotlinx-coroutines 1.9.0 (runtime only); Jetpack Compose Material 3 via BOM 2024.12.01 (UI only)
decisions.value: agents-core and agents-fs use only the Kotlin standard library. agents-runtime uses kotlinx-coroutines 1.9.0. agents-ui uses Compose BOM 2024.12.01 with Material 3.
decisions.reason: Same versions as the host app; no new frameworks introduced.

decisions.title: Platform: Android minSdk 26, compileSdk 35, targetSdk 35; core and fs modules target the JVM
decisions.value: minSdk 26, compileSdk 35, targetSdk 35 (identical to app and core:android).
decisions.reason: Verified in app/build.gradle.kts and core/android/build.gradle.kts.

decisions.title: Build: Gradle with the Anvex version catalog (AGP 8.7.3, KSP 2.0.21-1.0.28)
decisions.value: Gradle wrapper of Anvex 4.15.2; versions taken only from gradle/libs.versions.toml; no new repositories (FAIL_ON_PROJECT_REPOS stays).
decisions.reason: Compatibility with the existing build and release workflows.

decisions.title: Runtime: JVM 17 bytecode for core modules; Android ART for runtime/ui modules
decisions.value: JVM 17 target, no preview language features.
decisions.reason: Host app uses JavaVersion.VERSION_17.

decisions.title: Toolchain: JDK 17 for Gradle builds; kotlinc 2.0.21 for standalone verification of JVM modules
decisions.value: Official builds use JDK 17. Standalone verification compiles with kotlinc 2.0.21 and -jvm-target 17 on any JDK >= 17.
decisions.reason: Lets agents-core and agents-fs be verified without Gradle; the Gradle build remains the authoritative build.

decisions.title: Database: Room 2.6.1 with KSP, in a separate database file agents.db
decisions.value: Own AgentsDatabase (agents.db) with its own migration chain and schema snapshots. Cross-reference to Anvex projects by projectId string only.
decisions.reason: Keeps the module removable and the integration free of changes to AnvexDatabase.

decisions.title: Dependency injection: manual constructor injection through an AgentsGraph; no DI framework
decisions.value: AgentsGraph is constructed by the host AppGraph with the adapters of ARC-INT-1.
decisions.reason: Anvex AppGraph is a manual DI graph; no DI framework is present.

decisions.title: Networking: the module opens no network connections; model calls go through the host ProviderClient (OkHttp 4.12.0 in core:ai)
decisions.value: No HTTP client dependency in any agents module. AgentRunnerPort in agents-runtime obtains a ProviderClient from the host through ProviderPort.
decisions.reason: Provider independence and a single credential handling path.

decisions.title: Testing: JUnit 4.13.2 and kotlinx-coroutines-test 1.9.0; JVM modules must be runnable without Android
decisions.value: JUnit 4.13.2 (same as libs.versions.toml). Tests of agents-core and agents-fs run on the plain JVM.
decisions.reason: Matches existing test stack.

decisions.title: The module has its own parallel scheduler; DurableTaskEngine is used only as a pattern
decisions.value: DurableTaskEngine.drain() holds workerMutex and joins each task, so tasks run strictly one at a time. The module schedules in parallel itself and persists to agents.db.
decisions.reason: Verified in core/android .../reliability/DurableTaskEngine.kt.

decisions.title: The module does not reuse ChatSession; the runner composes ProviderClient, BoltStreamParser, ActionDispatcher and PatchEngine
decisions.value: No change to ChatSession (1525 lines) or HarnessBridge (1232 lines). ActionDispatcher receives a ProjectFileSystem view of the agent workspace.
decisions.reason: ChatSession is coupled to chat persistence and UI state; both are known technical debt in CHANGELOG.

decisions.title: PFP is a development-time standard; the in-app Policy Engine implements the semantics of the PFP Runtime Enforcement Contract
decisions.value: No PFP code ships in the app. Rules (fail-closed, DENY precedence, evidence chain, no implicit ALLOW) are implemented in code in ARC-SEC-1 and recorded in ARC-SEC-3.
decisions.reason: PFP v5.7.7 is specification plus Python validators and states that it is not a runtime.

decisions.title: Integration touches the main source only at the listed contract points
decisions.value: Allowed edits: settings.gradle.kts (include lines), app dependency lines, AppGraph wiring, one navigation route and entry point, string resources (en, fa), source-mirror regeneration. Any other edit requires a new ADR.
decisions.reason: Directive: build the module completely, then add it at the end.

decisions.title: Competing implementations of one task are compared by the user; they are never auto-merged with each other
decisions.value: Each competitor has its own fork. Selecting one result integrates only that ChangeSet.
decisions.reason: Merging two independent solutions to the same problem produces incoherent code.

decisions.title: Autonomous Project Manager is DEFERRED; milestone 5 ships a manager that only proposes a plan
decisions.reason: Task decomposition and delegation quality must be proven on user-managed teams first.
decisions.fallback: User-managed teams (Mode B); the manager proposes a task graph that the user approves.
decisions.acceptance: Manager-created plans are accepted by users without edits in at least 8 of 10 benchmark objectives, and gates remain non-bypassable.

decisions.title: Agent profile import/export is DEFERRED
decisions.reason: Needs a versioned profile schema and credential-stripping rules; not needed for MVP.
decisions.fallback: Profiles are created in the UI and stored in agents.db; JSON export is not offered.
decisions.acceptance: Exported profile contains no credential material and re-imports byte-identically.

decisions.title: SAF import/export gateway is DEFERRED; SAF-backed projects are unsupported in v1
decisions.reason: Gateway needs its own UX (copy-in, copy-out, conflict on export) and must not influence the core design.
decisions.fallback: Team creation on a SAF-backed project fails closed with an explanatory message.
decisions.acceptance: A SAF project is copied to an app-private real workspace, worked on, and exported back; the engine never receives a content:// URI.

decisions.title: Default maximum concurrent agents
decisions.reason: Depends on measured memory and rate-limit behavior on target devices.
decisions.resolver: Product owner with M3 device measurements
decisions.impactIfUnresolved: Implementation uses 3 as a configurable default; users can change it, so work is not blocked.

decisions.title: Default review policy for low-risk changes
decisions.reason: Automatic approval of low-risk changes is requested by the vision, but a risk classifier does not exist yet.
options: Auto-approve when all checks pass and the diff is under a size limit
decisions.impactIfUnresolved: M5 ships with the independent reviewer always required, which is the safe default.

decisions.title: The Orchestrator that executes scheduler commands lives in agents-core; the Android layer is only an asynchronous shell around it
decisions.value: Orchestrator (core, pure JVM) forks workspaces, vets agent output, selects an independent reviewer, applies change sets through the Integrator and persists events write-ahead. RunLauncher is the only asynchronous seam; CoroutineRunLauncher in agents-runtime starts coroutines and reports results as events.
decisions.reason: Lets the whole flow (run, review, merge, crash recovery) be proven with plain JVM tests; verified by 203 core tests.

decisions.title: Events are persisted write-ahead as canonical JSON and the hash chain covers that JSON, not toString
decisions.value: EventCodec defines a strict, versioned JSON form of every scheduler event. An event is appended to the store BEFORE it changes state; a store failure drops the event and changes nothing. EventLog hashes seq|prevHash|canonical JSON. Free text is scrubbed of credentials before persisting and GuardedEventStore refuses credential-like payloads.
decisions.reason: Data-class toString is not a stable format; replay must reproduce the exact state.

decisions.title: After a restart interrupted work is redone: a Requeue event returns the task to RevisionRequired without consuming an attempt; a write-ahead apply journal repairs a half-applied project
decisions.value: ApplyJournal.started(task, rollbackSnapshot) is durable before the first workspace write. On restart ApplyRecovery restores the snapshot, then Orchestrator.reconcile() requeues every task that was Assigned, InProgress, UnderReview or waiting for the user. Forks of the dead process are not reused.
decisions.reason: Review verdicts and change sets live in process memory; redoing is simpler and safer than persisting them in this version.

decisions.title: RelPath accepts only the canonical form: a string is valid exactly when the host PathSanitizer returns it unchanged and it is at most 4096 characters
decisions.value: RelPath.parse(x) is non-null <=> PathSanitizer.sanitizeOrNull(x) == x and x.length <= 4096. Verified on 180000 generated inputs. Finding: the host sanitizer is not idempotent (for example it rewrites ./C:/x to C:/x, whose own sanitization would reject it); RelPath refuses such outputs and agents-fs fails closed on workspace names it cannot represent, except inside ignored areas.
decisions.reason: Stricter than the host by design for untrusted agent output.

decisions.title: agents-fs is an Android library module only so that its tests can use the host RealProjectFileSystem; its main code uses no Android API
decisions.value: com.android.library with testImplementation(project(':core:android')); FsArchitectureGuardTest keeps main sources free of File, Uri, DocumentFile, ContentResolver and Android imports.
decisions.reason: RealProjectFileSystem lives in an Android library; a plain JVM module cannot depend on it.

acceptanceTests.title: Independent tasks run in parallel; dependent tasks wait for their prerequisites
Tasks whose declared file claims overlap are serialized; disjoint tasks run together
Number of running agents never exceeds the configured cap under a stress sequence
Exhausting a token or cost budget stops new work and cancels running agents
Replaying the event log reproduces the exact scheduler state after a simulated crash
Traversal, absolute, NUL, bidi and symlink paths are rejected by RelPath and the real filesystem
Restoring a snapshot reproduces every file byte for byte and detects a corrupted blob
Writes in a fork never change the base workspace or another fork
Malformed, oversized, traversal and sensitive-path ChangeSets are rejected before any write
Non-overlapping edits from two agents merge automatically and correctly
Overlapping or adjacent edits produce a conflict and no file is modified
Binary, CRLF, delete-vs-edit and add-in-both cases behave exactly as the edge-case table states
Applying a ChangeSet whose base is stale never overwrites newer content
A failure injected mid-apply restores the pre-apply snapshot
A change outside the task write grant is denied or escalated, never applied silently
A task cannot reach Verified without a review by a different agent or the user
Approval messages from the manager or the author do not satisfy a mandatory gate
A scan of agents.db, event log, audit trail and prompts finds no credential material
Static scan of agents-core finds no java.io.File, Uri, DocumentFile or ContentResolver
A SAF-backed project is refused at team creation with a clear message
After a simulated process kill, interrupted runs resume or are marked interrupted without data loss
Cancelling a team cancels all agents and releases their workspaces
The same run succeeds with a fake provider and with two different real provider kinds
UI shows each agent's status, files touched, decisions, tokens and remaining work
User can compare two competing results side by side and choose one
Manager output is a plan that cannot start without explicit user approval
Anvex release audit scripts pass with the module integrated
A diff of the main source touches only the files listed in the integration contract
Context sent to an agent stays within its configured size and excludes unrelated files
A process kill at any step of an apply is repaired on restart: the project equals its pre-apply state and the task is redone
Unusable agent output never reaches review: it becomes a retryable failure and is never integrated
A new agent role is added by registering a profile without modifying scheduler or integrator code

scopeDecisions.original: PFP must remain the authoritative governance layer.
scopeDecisions.proposed: PFP stays authoritative as the development-time standard (this package and its validators); the in-app Policy Engine implements the semantics of the PFP Runtime Enforcement Contract in code.
scopeDecisions.reason: PFP v5.7.7 is specification plus Python validators and declares itself not a runtime; there is no PFP code to embed in the app.
scopeDecisions.impact: Governance of generated code is enforced by PFP gates; runtime governance of agent actions is enforced by ARC-SEC-1.

scopeDecisions.original: Git branches and Git Worktrees where supported.
scopeDecisions.proposed: Isolated workspaces are CAS-backed forks; merging is performed by the in-module Integrator.
scopeDecisions.reason: GitLite offers one working tree and no merge; worktrees are not supported on this platform ('where supported' applies).
scopeDecisions.impact: Same isolation and conflict goals without Git worktrees.
scopeDecisions.decision: Use forks and three-way merge (ADR-005, ADR-006).

scopeDecisions.original: A central Project Manager Agent manages a team of specialized subordinate agents.
scopeDecisions.proposed: Milestone 5 ships a manager that only proposes a task graph requiring user approval; autonomous management is deferred.
scopeDecisions.reason: Delegation quality must be proven on user-managed teams, and gates must remain non-bypassable.
scopeDecisions.impact: Mode A is partial in the first release.

scopeDecisions.proposed: Deferred until a credential-free profile schema exists.

risks.title: Merge or integrator defect silently corrupts user code
risks.mitigation: Conservative policy, property tests, fault injection, deep review
risks.trigger: Any change to merge or integrator

risks.title: Android process death during a run
risks.mitigation: Event log replay, atomic apply, Interrupted state
risks.contingency: Resume or discard run from persisted state

risks.title: Cost overrun from parallel agents
risks.mitigation: Hard caps, 80 percent warning, cost shown before start

risks.title: Host API drift between baseline 4.15.2 and the final integration
risks.mitigation: Adapters at the composition root; re-verify signatures at M6

risks.title: Android layers cannot be verified in the planning sandbox
risks.mitigation: Label UNVERIFIED; verify on real tooling before acceptance
risks.contingency: Do not close the milestone until built and run

risks.title: Device memory or rate limits reduce usable concurrency
risks.mitigation: Configurable cap; decide default with measurements (ADR-028)

migrationPlan.currentState: Anvex 4.15.2 is a multi-module Android app (core:model, core:engine, core:ai, core:android, app) with a single-agent chat engine, a harness web UI, Room database version 13 and a manual DI graph.
migrationPlan.targetState: Anvex gains a separable multi-agent module (four Gradle modules) integrated only at contract points.
migrationPlan.strategy: Build the module completely in a copy of Anvex 4.15.2, then integrate at the listed contract points.
migrationPlan.rollback: Remove the include lines, dependency lines, graph wiring, route and strings; agents.db is separate and can be deleted without affecting anvex.db.

observability.logging: Structured local logs with identifiers, sizes and digests; no file contents, prompts or credentials.
observability.metrics: Per-agent and per-task tokens, cost, run duration, conflict count, retry count.
observability.tracing: Run and task IDs propagate through events and audit records.
observability.auditEvents: Every state transition, policy decision, gate verdict, apply, rollback and budget stop.
observability.healthChecks: Startup recovery check of persisted runs and CAS integrity sampling.
observability.alerts: User notifications for conflicts, gates awaiting a decision, budget at 80 percent and interrupted runs.
observability.slo: No accepted ChangeSet lost and no half-applied workspace after a process kill.
observability.sli: Count of recovery anomalies and of blob verification failures per 1000 runs.
